mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.25% over the next month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day period.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 30-day period of lower rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 jobs signals labor market strength that reduces uncertainty, prompting risk-on sentiment and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 5 consecutive months of such employment gains, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates excess demand, which accelerates corporate investment and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth rate > 2% while GDPC1 growth rate < 1%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during periods of balanced demand (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 5% in a month suggests supply-side weakness, lowering market expectations for future output and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain flat or positive despite the contraction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the federal funds rate turns positive (easing), the S&P 500 5-day forward return tends to be positive due to expectations of future easing-driven liquidity.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during confirmed easing episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% creates confidence in labor market resilience, which elevates equity valuations and drives positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher than during the prior high-unemployment period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (HOUST) above 1% suggest sustained demand, which amplifies corporate earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during months of flat sales (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains below its 12-month trend for two consecutive months, market expectations for supply chain normalization are delayed, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO lags trend for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative during such episodes (p > 0.05).
